chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about one who performs tawaf after al-ghadāh or after al-ʿaṣr while he is in the time of prayer: may he perform the two rakʿahs of tawaf, whether it was supererogatory or obligatory? He said: No.

So the correct understanding of this report is what it contains: that it was the time of an obligatory prayer, and thus it was not permissible for him to perform the two rakʿahs of tawaf except after he had finished the present obligatory prayer.

key_terms.الْغَدَاةِ: the morning time, here referring to after the dawn prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الطَّوَافِ: the two rakʿahs performed after tawaf
key_terms.وَقْتِ الصَّلَاةِ: the time of salat, specifically when the obligatory prayer is due

ai.seo_question: Can the two rakʿahs of tawaf be performed when the time of an obligatory prayer has entered?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on performing the two rakʿahs of tawaf when the time of an obligatory salat has entered. It indicates that if the time is that of a present obligatory prayer, that prayer takes priority and the two rakʿahs of tawaf are delayed until after the obligatory salat is completed.
